abstract_ko: 본 연구는 아랍어 작문 과제 수행 상황에서 인공지능 도구 사용의 효과성을 탐색하고 상호작용 유형을 정리하여 이에 영향을 미치는 아랍어 학습자 특성과 상호작용 유형에 따른 수행 결과를 확인하고자 하였다. 인공지능 번역기를 사용하는 아랍어 작문 과정에서 나타나는 학습자의 행동별 시간 비율을 기반으로 군집분석을 실시한 결과, 제한적-한국어형, 제한적-아랍어형, 협력적 유형의 세 가지 유형이 나타났다. 제한적-한국어형은 학습자 단독 행동 중 한국어 작문의 행동 비율이 가장 높게 나타났으며, 제한적-아랍어형은 학습자 단독 행동 중 아랍어 작문 행동의 비율이 가장 높게 나타났다. 협력적 유형은 다른 두 유형과는 달리 한국어 작문과 아랍어 작문의 비율 차이가 크지 않았으며, 번역기와의 상호작용적 작문 활동 비율이 가장 높게 나타났다. 인공지능 번역기를 사용하는 과정에서 나타나는 행동 시간 비율에서도 확인할 수 있듯이 세 유형 간에는 명확한 차이가 존재하였다. 면담 분석에서는 이러한 차이를 보다 구체적으로 확인할 수 있었다. 제한적-한국어형 유형은 한국어로 전체 글을 작성한 후 번역기에 입력하는 이유로 초안 작성 단계에서 인공지능 번역기가 신뢰할 만하다고 응답하였다. 반대로, 제한적-아랍어형 유형은 초벌 번역 단계에서 학습자가 단독으로 아랍어 작문을 시도한 후 필요에 따라 인공지능 번역기를 활용하며, 그 이유는 표현의 정교화나 모르는 표현을 확인하기 위함이라고 응답하였다. 마지막으로 협력적 상호작용 유형의 학습자들은 아랍어 작문 내용 중 중요한 부분은 자신들이 주도적으로 작문하되, 상대적으로 중요도가 낮거나 부연 설명 목적의 문장은 인공지능 번역기에 맡긴다고 응답하였다. 또한, 이 유형의 학습자들은 인공지능 번역기와의 상호작용에서 소통 방식을 고려하여 번역할 내용을 입력하였다고도 응답하였다. 본 연구에서는 인공지능 및 아랍어 작문 관련 역량이 학습자와 인공지능의 상호작용 유형에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 확인하고자 하였다. 연구 결과 상호작용 유형별로 인공지능 관련 역량의 집단별 차이는 유의하지 않았으나, 아랍어 작문 역량의 차이는 유의하게 나타났다. 특히 제한적-아랍어형 유형은 다른 두 유형보다 통제집단의 인지된 수행 결과 점수 및 아랍어 작문 자기 효능감이 유의하게 높았다. 이를 통해 학습자의 교과지식이 높을수록 인공지능 도구에 대한 의존도가 낮아질 수 있음을 추측할 수 있다. 또한, 학습자의 유형에 따른 아랍어 작문 결과를 비교한 결과, 통계적으로 유의미한 차이는 나타나지 않았다. 기술 통계 분석에서는 협력적 유형의 내용 점수 향상이 가장 높았으며, 제한적-한국어형은 표현 점수와 전체 점수, 인지된 수행 결과의 향상이 가장 높게 나타났다. 반면 제한적-아랍어형은 모든 영역에서 향상도가 가장 낮게 나타났다.

title_ko: The Role of Prompt Language in ChatGPT-Assisted Revision: Effects on Korean EFL Argumentative Writing
title_en: The Role of Prompt Language in ChatGPT-Assisted Revision: Effects on Korean EFL Argumentative Writing
kw_en: ChatGPT; prompt language; argumentative writing; revision strategies; EFL learners
abstract_ko: This study investigates how Korean EFL university students revised their argumentative essays using ChatGPT, with a focus on how prompt language (English vs. Korean) and specificity influenced the nature and uptake of AI-generated feedback. Drawing on analyses of revised texts and prompts students used, the findings reveal that English prompts more frequently led to global-level changes, such as improved organization, argument clarity, and academic tone. In contrast, Korean prompts typically resulted in sentence-level edits, including lexical refinement and fluency improvement. Across both languages, prompt specificity emerged as a key factor: students who provided clear, goal-oriented instructions received more relevant and actionable feedback. While learners generally valued ChatGPT’s support in enhancing expression and correcting grammar, some expressed concerns about loss of authorial voice and over-dependence on AI tools. These results underscore the need to develop students’ prompt literacy and critical awareness when integrating AI into academic writing instruction.

title_ko: Examining the Effectiveness of Generative AI as a Bilingual Dictionary in Korean EFL Contexts
title_en: Examining the Effectiveness of Generative AI as a Bilingual Dictionary in Korean EFL Contexts
kw_en: second language acquisition; computer assisted language learning; dictionary use; generative AI; reading comprehension; vocabulary acquisition
abstract_ko: Large Language Model-based generative AI has the potential to change language education, as it is able to parse natural language prompts and provide natural-seeming responses to these prompts. To date, there has been little research into generative AI as a tool to assist language learners in reading comprehension and vocabulary acquisition. This paper presents an experimental study that compares the effectiveness of ChatGPT to the online bilingual NAVER Dictionary and to a control group in both a reading comprehension/written recall task and a vocabulary acquisition test using both the Vocabulary Knowledge Scale test and a multiple choice meaning test. The subjects were 120 Korean undergraduate students majoring in English Language and Literature. ANOVA results of pausal units and target vocabulary recalled during the written recall task suggest that a dedicated bilingual dictionary is superior to ChatGPT for reading comprehension, but AI can assist learners to identify unknown words just as well. For vocabulary acquisition, ANOVA results on both vocabulary measures show both ChatGPT and NAVER Dictionary groups significantly outperformed the control group, with no differences between the two dictionary groups. This suggests that ChatGPT may be an adequate substitute for a bilingual dictionary and a useful tool for language learners to improve vocabulary.

abstract_ko: The purpose of this research is to investigate the impact of generative AI on Korean secondary English education, following the emergence of ChatGPT in 2022. Generative AI is predominantly used for reading and writing, a trend influenced by Korea’s assessment environment and AI’s technical capabilities and user accessibility. Research reveals that AI tools have differential effects based on proficiency; they significantly improve the language skills and confidence of low/intermediate-level students, potentially reducing learning gaps and implying the need for differentiated pedagogical strategies. The introduction of AI is also shifting the teacher’s role from a knowledge transmitter to a learning designer and facilitator. Furthermore, learners tend to adopt self-directed methods by using AI as an interactive partner for designing questions and revising work based on feedback. Overall, generative AI is a powerful tool for innovative pedagogical approaches and learner-centered education. To maximize its potential, future research should focus on developing integrated models that better incorporate competency-based learning models, redefining the teacher’s role, and creating new assessment methods for the AI era.

abstract_ko: This study aims to phenomenologically explore the effects of ChatGPT-based English writing activities using the familiar story of Peter Pan with university students. Eight participants engaged in a structured writing activity and were later interviewed using semi-structured protocols to capture their subjective experiences. Data were analyzed following Colaizzi’s phenomenological method. The results revealed four essential themes: emotional stability, improvement in cognitive strategies, enhanced linguistic performance, and perceived limitations. ChatGPT contributed to emotional relief and facilitated the use of metacognitive strategies such as self-reflection and self-correction. Participants also reported improvements in expression and writing quality. However, concerns were raised about the potential decline in independent thinking due to frequent reliance on AI. Based on these findings, pedagogical suggestions for integrating AI feedback into university English writing instruction are discussed.

title_en: Comparison of Human and ChatGPT on Holistic and Analytic Scoring of College EFL Opinion Writing

abstract_ko: Writing evaluation can be done using different approaches such as holistic and analytic scoring, and by different raters, including human raters and machine. This study investigated the inter-rater reliability in holistic and analytic scoring by human raters and ChatGPT and the associations between average scores assigned by the two raters. Data consisted of one-paragraph opinion essays (n = 196) written by 28 South Korean college freshmen, which were scored by two human raters and ChatGPT across two trials. Inter-rater reliability, independent-samples t-tests, and correlations were computed. Results indicated that both humans and ChatGPT demonstrated substantial consistency, with humans showing greater reliability in holistic judgments, while ChatGPT exhibited stronger reliability in analytic categories of language and organization. Holistic scores did not differ significantly between the two raters; however, humans tended to be stricter in content and organization, whereas ChatGPT was stricter in language and mechanics. Strong correlations across all scores further suggested that humans and ChatGPT produced comparable rank-order evaluations. Overall, these findings support the theoretical validity of incorporating AI into writing assessment and highlight its pedagogical potential as a complement to human raters in EFL writing evaluation.

abstract_ko: This study presents a systematic review of empirical research on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in English education published between 30 November 2022 and December 2024, covering 50 studies. The review identifies the predominant generative AI tools, their educational functions, and recent trends in their evolution. Results show that ChatGPT is overwhelmingly dominant, appearing in 56% of studies, yet 54% of them did not specify the model version, raising serious concerns regarding reproducibility. Reported functions include pronunciation analysis, interactive dialogue, vocabulary support, automated writing evaluation, idea generation, and machine translation, with applications supporting integrated language functions showing notably higher adoption rates. The findings further highlight the rapid advancement of AI capabilities, particularly in processing speed, accuracy, and multimodal functionality. These results underscore the necessity of detailed reporting on AI model versions and experimental conditions to ensure reproducibility and to establish standardized guidelines for AI-enhanced educational research.

kw_en: artificial intelligence; chatbot; human teacher; English education; learner perception; collaboration
abstract_ko: With the rapid advancement of artificially intelligent (AI) technology, its applications are expanding across various sectors of society. The field of English education is no exception, witnessing a swift integration of AI tools. In this context, this study empirically examined teachers’ (n = 107) and learners’ (n = 147) perceptions of the complementary roles of AI chatbots and human instructors in English education. Using both one-sample and independent-sample t-tests, this study revealed that teachers rated the usefulness of chatbots significantly higher than students, although both groups recognized their value for grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation support. Teachers also perceived chatbot limitations more strongly, stressing their insufficiency in emotional support and motivation. Both groups rated human teachers’ roles very highly, with teachers showing stronger awareness of pedagogical and affective functions. While learners acknowledged teachers’ indispensability, they also recognized the supportive role of AI. Finally, both groups expressed positive attitudes toward a collaborative instructional model, viewing AI and human instructors not as substitutes but as complementary partners in language learning.

abstract_ko: This year-long exploratory study examines an AI-supported personalized reading approach aimed at improving low student engagement. Conducted with 63 secondgrade high school students in a rural area, the researcher, a high school English teacher, utilized AI to generate engaging reading passages at various proficiency levels. Students were allowed to choose texts that best matched their abilities. A mixedmethods design was employed, collecting mock test scores to identify achievement trends and using comparative surveys to evaluate student perceptions compared to the previous grammar-translation method. The findings revealed a positive trend in academic achievement, marked by a decrease in low-level students and an increase in middle and high-level students. Additionally, students reported a significant improvement in their learning experience compared to the prior method, demonstrating much higher levels of satisfaction, motivation, and interest with the new approach. Notably, the autonomy students had in selecting passages successfully preserved their self-esteem, addressing a key challenge in traditional ability grouping. While acknowledging its exploratory nature and context-specific limitations, this research presents a practical model for revitalizing secondary English education and offers a rare long-term perspective on AI integration in an authentic K-12 classroom.

abstract_ko: This study analyzed error patterns in the English writing of Korean EFL learners using ChatGPT and examined their pedagogical impli- cations. A total of 150 errors were identified from student writing samples, with the most frequent involving grammar errors followed by awkward phrasing, collocation, and structural errors. Many of these errors reflected Korean linguistic features such as the absence of articles and plural markers, as well as reliance on literal translation and limited exposure to authentic English. To address these challenges, the study proposes a multi- dimensional approach that combines explicit grammar instruction, contrastive analysis, data-driven learning, and context-based practice. A key contribution of this research lies in demonstrating the effectiveness of AI-powered tools like ChatGPT: it not only supported learners in recognizing and understanding errors but also provided instructors with diagnostic insights for targeted teaching. While AI cannot replace human feedback, it shows strong potential as a supplementary resource for improving accuracy in EFL writing.

abstract_ko: This study explores the effects of English listening instruction that integrates TED-Ed video content with ChatGPT-based learning activities on EFL university students' listening achievement and listening self-efficacy. A 15-week instructional model was designed to promote learners' strategic engagement through sentence analysis, vocabulary expansion, and shadowing. ChatGPT was utilized as an interactive learning partner to provide personalized feedback, extend expressions, and support self-regulated learning. Quantitative data from pre- and post-tests showed significant improvement in both listening comprehension and listening self-efficacy. In addition, qualitative responses from open-ended questionnaires indicated that students experienced improved strategy awareness, and stronger motivation for continued listening practice. These findings suggest that integrating generative AI with educational videos is an effective approach to fostering interactive and strategy-based listening instruction in EFL settings.

abstract_ko: This study investigates whether ChatGPT can recognize the affective force of aegyo, a Korean speech style marked by playful phonological alternations such as nasalization, affrication, and /j/-insertion. More specifically, it examines whether ChatGPT detects aegyo forms as “cuter” than their canonical counterparts and whether it can distinguish degrees of cuteness based on phonological features and phonotactic acceptability, following Jang (2021). Three ChatGPT versions (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o) rated 11 verbs in seven conditions on a 7-point scale. Results showed that aegyo forms were rated as cuter, indicating sensitivity to affective cues. However, internal rankings diverged from human judgments: while humans favored forms aligned with phonotactic constraints—especially affrication and stopping—ChatGPT prioritized /j/-insertion. Version-specific trends appeared: GPT-3.5 gave conservative scores, GPT-4 moderate contrasts, and GPT-4o stronger contrasts with greater variability, suggesting partial but limited sociophonetic sensitivity.

title_ko: The effect of teacher-led scaffolding on Korean EFL adolescents’ writing engagement with AI writing feedback
title_en: The effect of teacher-led scaffolding on Korean EFL adolescents’ writing engagement with AI writing feedback
kw_en: AI Feedback; EFL Writing; Teacher Scaffolding; Metacognitive Engagement; Adolescent Learners
abstract_ko: As generative AI tools increasingly enter EFL classrooms, their role in supporting young learners’ writing development requires closer examination. This study explored the effects of AI-generated feedback on the writing revision process and outcomes of Korean middle school EFL students, with a particular focus on the mediating role of teacher scaffolding. A quasi-experimental mixed-methods design was employed with two instructional conditions: AI-only (where participants received only AI feedback) and AI+teacher scaffolding (where participants obtained both AI feedbacks and teacher scaffolding). Eighteen middle students participated in the study. Data sources included original and revised drafts, analytic rubric scores, metacognitive awareness surveys, and post-intervention interviews. Findings indicated that the AI-only group tended to apply suggestions at a surface level, while the AI+teacher scaffolding group was engaged in more strategic and reflective revisions. The AI+teacher group demonstrated greater gains in writing quality—particularly in vocabulary use and grammatical accuracy—and reported higher levels of metacognitive and emotional engagement. These findings suggest that while AI feedback provides immediate corrective input, its instructional value is significantly enhanced when embedded within teacher-led scaffolding that promotes critical thinking, self-regulation, and learner autonomy.

abstract_ko: This study explores middle school English teachers’ experiences and perceptions of using AI digital textbooks (AIDT) during the first semester of 2025. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the research conducted surveys and in-depth interviews with eight teachers who actively used AIDT in their classes across diverse regional contexts including Seoul, Gyeonggi, Daegu, and Jeonnam. Data were analyzed through content analysis and thematic analysis to examine classroom changes, core function utilization, effectiveness across language skills, and implementation challenges. The findings reveal that AIDT enhanced student participation and individualized learning, particularly benefiting underachieving students. Additionally, AIDT led to diverse teacher role identities including instructional designers, facilitators, and managers. Among core functions, teacher customization received the highest evaluation, whereas AI tutor functions were rated least favorably. Regarding language skills, speaking activities demonstrated the highest perceived effectiveness, while reading showed little advantage over traditional textbooks. Implementation challenges identified by teachers encompassed technical infrastructure limitations, complex administrative procedures, rushed policy rollout, teacher-related factors, and significant quality disparities among publishers. The study concludes that while AIDT holds promise for enhancing personalized learning and student engagement, addressing the identified challenges is essential to realizing its full potential in diverse educational contexts. abstract_ko: This study examines how the 2022 Revised English Curriculum’s core goals—digital literacy and self-directed learning—are implemented in the 2025 edition of first-year middle school English textbooks in South Korea. The analysis reveals that while all textbooks share a general structure combining integrated language skill activities with project tasks, their pedagogical orientations diverge: some have adopted a theme-based structure, whereas others have retained skill-based formats. As for digital literacy, although digital resources are consistently accessible via QR codes, their depth of integration varies considerably, and AI-driven feedback functions are absent. In terms of learner autonomy, only a limited number of textbooks provide explicit opportunities for choice or scaffolds for self-regulated learning. These findings suggest a partial but uneven realization of curriculum intention and thus a need for stronger alignment between curriculum goals and textbook design by expanding functional digital integration beyond basic access.

abstract_ko: The purpose of this study was to explore the perceptions of university students who used ChatGPT for English learning and to analyze how these factors affected their learning motivation and achievement experiences. To achieve this research purpose, a mixed-methods approach was employed with data collected from 63 undergraduates in Gyeonggi-do, South Korea. Quantitative data were processed using SPSS 27 employing descriptive statistics, t-tests, multivariate analysis, Mann-Whitney U test, and regression; qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis based on students’ responses to open-ended questions. The findings revealed that higher-grade students used ChatGPT more actively, and perceptions of ChatGPT significantly affected self-directed language learning depending on academic division. Qualitative results also highlighted enhanced efficiency in goal setting and task completion although some noted the risks of over-reliance. This study suggests the need for structured educational strategies to promote balanced and effective use of ChatGPT in English learning.

abstract_ko: This study examined the impact of college student’s engagement with ChatGPT-based speaking assignments on their speaking proficiency and perceptions of AI-assisted learning. A comparative analysis was conducted between high and low-engagement groups, excluding mid-engagement participants. Students completed ChatGPT-based speaking assignments twice a week over nine weeks, and both quantitative and qualitative data were collected. Paired samples t-tests indicated significant improvement in Responding to Questions and Expressing an Opinion for both the high- and low-engagement groups. In contrast, independent samples t-tests revealed that the high-engagement group significantly outperformed the low engagement group in overall speaking performance on the post-tests across both speaking tasks. These findings suggest that consistent participation meaningfully contributes to language development. Additionally, student’s perceptions of ChatGPT differed by engagement level. While low-engagement students acknowledged its convenience and emotional support, high engagement students reported enhanced confidence, reduced anxiety, and greater satisfaction with the learning process. Qualitative responses further highlighted differences in perceived strengths and limitations of AI, as well as preferences for human versus AI instruction. The results underscore the pedagogical potential of structured, AI-integrated speaking tasks and the crucial role of sustained engagement in maximizing both cognitive and affective learning outcomes.

abstract_ko: This study investigates the effectiveness of integrating ChatGPT- assisted translation-judgment tasks into inductive grammar learning for EFL students. Participants evaluated a series of English–Korean translations of passive-voice sentences generated by ChatGPT and completed a reflective survey about their learning experience. Findings revealed that students generally demonstrated a strong ability to recognize correct and incorrect uses of the passive voice, though they encountered greater difficulty when sentences included multiple grammatical features, such as the combination of progressive and passive forms. Qualitative results showed that learners developed heightened awareness of grammatical patterns, and increased motivation for self-directed learning. Many participants also expressed a more critical understanding of AI-generated translations, recognizing both their usefulness and their limitations. When used as a scaffold for guided comparison and reasoning, ChatGPT supports learners in discovering rules through analysis, offering a practical and engaging model for modern EFL grammar instruction.

abstract_ko: The objective of this study was to identify the key themes and topics addressed in recent research on AI-assisted writing tools in English education. Additionally, the study aimed to examine the research methods and participant groups commonly used in the selected studies, explore the reported pedagogical benefits and challenges, and consider the implications of the findings for language teachers, curriculum designers, and policymakers. To collect data, journal articles were retrieved from the Research Information Service System(RISS), and a total of 16 articles were selected through a multi-stage screening process. The data were analyzed using constant comparison, thematic analysis, and inter-coder reliability to ensure the trustworthiness of the findings. Through this process, five key themes emerged. In terms of pedagogical impact, the findings highlight several benefits, including improvements in grammar, vocabulary, coherence, and overall writing quality—particularly among students who received AI-generated feedback. However, a major challenge identified is the risk of overreliance on AI, which may hinder the development of students’ independent writing and critical thinking skills. The study concludes with a discussion of implications for educational practice and policy, as well as the limitations of the current research.

On the other hand, Activity B was an activity that repeats the process of creating and modifying prompts until learners obtained the desired image, and the generated visual stimulation served as the starting point for language activities. This process induced learners' spontaneous and creative expression and encouraged the experience of constructing utterances while moving back and forth between language and thought. In addition, the multi-step feedback generated during the generation process provided an opportunity for learners to visually recognize their learning progress and sense of accomplishment. Furthermore, the process of creating and correcting prompts in Japanese after organizing thoughts in the native language promoted the application of expressive and grammatical knowledge and showed results that increased learners' subjectivity. From the above, it was revealed that conversation activities using image generation AI have effectiveness as a new teaching and learning model that can foster learners' creativity and subjectivity in beginner Japanese conversation classes.

abstract_ko: The Journal of Studies in Language 00.0, 000-000. The main purpose of this study is to examine how EFL students develop and manifest a newly emerging concept of prompt literacy when interacting with generative AI(GenAI). Specifically, 43 undergraduate students participated in a project-based learning task that explored the sociocultural meanings and variations of English words or expressions by creating webtoons, short videos, or web pages with a help of GenAI. This study examined the whole process of their exploration, design and production, and sharing, enhanced by interactions with GenAI, peers, and the instructor. Though an in-depth analysis of qualitative date of students’ reflections and creation logs, this study examines how they conceptualized prompt literacy through two dimensions: ‘little p’ (micro and foundational level) and ‘Big P’ (macro and integrative level). Findings reveal that the ‘little p’ dimension involves skills of writing, reading, iteration, structuring, clarify, and contextual adjustment, while the ‘Big P’ dimension includes collaborative engagement, emergent creativity, multimodality, critical analysis, and ethical responsibility. More importantly, these two dimensions are interconnected and mutually complementary. Based on these findings, this study sheds new light on a dual model of prompt literacy and highlights the pedagogical importance of fostering cyclical development of foundational and integrative prompt literacy.

abstract_ko: The emergence of generative AI technologies, such as ChatGPT, is fundamentally reshaping educational landscapes, prompting urgent reconsideration of the teacher’s role. This study explores how teachers must reconceptualize their professional identity and instructional practices in the age of generative AI. Drawing on sociocultural theory and a comprehensive review of CALL and MALL literature, the paper argues that AI does not replace teachers but rather demands a structural transformation of their roles. Specifically, three core roles are proposed for teachers: prompt designer, critical mediator, and emotional and creative mentor. As prompt designers, teachers must master prompt literacy to co-create tailored learning materials with AI; as critical mediators, they safeguard against biases, misinformation, and ethical pitfalls; and as emotional and creative mentors, they nurture students’ motivation, creativity, and identity in ways AI cannot replicate. The study also highlights implications for teacher education programs and school systems, emphasizing the need for comprehensive AI literacy training and pedagogical innovation. Ultimately, the integration of generative AI offers opportunities to enrich learning experiences, provided that teachers actively lead its educational orchestration.

AI 텍스트는 명시적 저자의 부재, 알고리즘적 생성 과정의 불투명성, 그리고 정보의 사실적 불안정성이라는 구조적 특징을 지니며, 이는 독자에게 텍스트의 의미 이해를 넘어 사실 검증과 사회적 영향력 평가를 포함하는 확장된 해석 활동을 요청한다. 이에 본 연구는 Ⅱ장에서 AI 텍스트의 특성을 구체적으로 분석하고, 권력과 이데올로기 분석에 강점을 지닌 전통적 비판적 문식성이 정보의 비가시성과 유동성을 다루기에는 한계가 있음을 지적하였다. Ⅳ장에서는 이러한 논의를 사회문식성 관점으로 확장하여, 독자를 능동적 의미 구성자이자 사실 검증자, 그리고 정보 유통의 책임을 고려하는 윤리적 주체로 재위치시켰다. 결론적으로 본 연구는 AI 시대의 비판적 문식성을 의미 구성, 사실 검증, 사회적 책임을 포괄하는 실천적 문식성으로 재개념화할 것을 제안하며, 이는 새로운 독자 역량 정의와 비판적 문식성 교육의 방향 모색에 중요한 시사점을 제공한다.

abstract_ko: This mixed-methods study investigated Korean college EFL learners’ perceptions and behavioral intentions toward AI-enabled language learning applications. A survey based on the Technology Acceptance Model and Theory of Planned Behavior was administered to 196 Korean university students, with model validation using 370 Chinese students. Structural equation modeling revealed a six-factor model with Perceived Usefulness, Attitude toward AI Use, and Subjective Norm significantly predicting behavioral intention, explaining 68% of the variance. The analysis confirmed the importance of social factors and positive attitudes in AI adoption decisions. Qualitative findings revealed a significant attitude-behavior gap. The study highlights the need for targeted interventions to bridge the gap between current basic usage and AI’s pedagogical potential, emphasizing the importance of practical training and social support in promoting comprehensive AI adoption in Korean educational contexts.

abstract_ko: This study explored the impact of AI-supported instruction on the development of English communicative skills and ChatGPT literacy among Korean university students in an EFL context. Participants were divided into a control group (N = 25), who practiced speaking through face-toface conversations, and an experimental group (N = 26), who engaged in practice using ChatGPT. Data were collected through pre- and post-tests in speaking and listening, as well as surveys assessing ChatGPT literacy. While both groups showed significant within-group improvement in speaking and listening skills, no statistically significant differences between them. However, learners in the ChatGPT group demonstrated notably higher gains in speaking performance. Learners reported overall positive experiences, citing improved speaking skill, increased confidence, convenience, and engagement, while also noting limitations such as technical issues and occasional inaccuracies. These findings offer deeper insights into AI-integrated language instruction and highlight the importance of prompt literacy and pedagogical support in fostering autonomous learning in digital contexts.

abstract_ko: Score reporting plays an important role in supporting the validity of interpretations and uses of assessment results; however, it remains an underexplored topic particularly in domestic research contexts. This exploratory study examines how two user groups-students and teachers-understood and perceived a score report designed for an automated speaking assessment (ASA) system currently under development for Korean public education. A total of 224 Korean secondary school students completed an online survey measuring their understanding and perceptions. Five English teachers participated in online semi-structured interviews. Descriptive statistics, as well as group-independence chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests, on the survey responses showed that the students overall held low levels of understanding but positive perceptions with no significant differences between school levels and negligible effect sizes. A thematic analysis of the interview transcripts revealed that teachers appreciated individualized feedback on the analytic aspects of speaking performance presented through visual graphs. However, they expressed concerns that the written prose feedback was too general and some terminology lacked specificity for students, providing recommendations for improvement. These findings have implications for the development of a user-friendly score report that enhances the validity of assessment interpretations and uses.

abstract_ko: This study explored the impact of ChatGPT-assisted English instruction on high school students’ reading achievement and their perceptions of English learning. Fifty-six first-year high school students from two classes participated in the study over five weeks (20 class sessions) during one semester. Working in small groups, students collaboratively generated, shared, and reviewed ChatGPT-based questions related to reading comprehension, vocabulary, and grammar, providing explanations and peer feedback. Results from a paired-samples t-test indicated a statistically significant decrease in students’ English reading achievement after the intervention. Further analysis by proficiency level revealed that both high- and mid-level students showed significant declines, while low-level students exhibited no change. In contrast, analyses of pre- and post-survey data on students’ perceptions demonstrated a statistically significant increase in interest and confidence toward both English learning and reading, with the effect being particularly notable among mid-level learners. Post-study reflections suggested that students generally perceived the ChatGPT-integrated learning activities positively, although some reported technical challenges. These findings warrant further investigation into the cognitive and affective outcomes of integrating ChatGPT into English language instruction.

abstract_ko: This study investigates the efficacy of AI-based writing assistants in improving Korean writing skills among elementary students. Using a quasi-experimental design, 100 students were divided into experimental (AI tool users) and control groups (traditional methods). Over eight weeks, the AI group utilized Hangul Tutor, an adaptive platform providing real-time grammar checks, sentence restructuring suggestions, and gamified feedback. Post-tests revealed a 28% improvement in the AI group versus 12% in the control, with significant gains in structural coherence (p < 0.05). However, 15% of AI users exhibited reduced creativity, relying on automated corrections rather than original ideas. Results suggest AI enhances technical accuracy but requires balanced integration with teacher-led creative activities.

abstract_ko: This study investigates the efficacy of AI chatbots in enhancing English language proficiency, focusing on their role in vocabulary acquisition, grammar practice, and conversational fluency. A quasi-experimental design compared 120 learners using AI chatbots (Duolingo Max, Babbel) to a control group engaging in traditional classroom instruction. Over six weeks, chatbot users demonstrated a 22% improvement in vocabulary retention and a 15% gain in grammatical accuracy, with significant increases in confidence during spoken interactions (p < 0.05). However, 20% of participants reported reduced motivation due to the absence of human interaction. Qualitative feedback highlighted chatbots’ utility for self-paced learning but criticized their inability to contextualize cultural nuances. The findings advocate for AI chatbots as supplementary tools, emphasizing blended learning models to balance technological efficiency with human mentorship.

The study underscores the potential of incorporating Immersive Reader into English education to foster self-directed learning.

abstract_ko: This study investigates how core competencies—communication, creativity, and collaboration—are realized in Korean middle school English textbooks through AI-assisted analysis using ChatGPT. While previous textbook studies have largely relied on qualitative coding and researcher interpretation, this study addresses the methodological limitation by applying large-scale semantic network analysis. The data consist of two representative units selected from first-grade middle school English textbooks (2023–2025 editions) published by YBM, Chunjae, and Visang. ChatGPT was employed to conduct semantic similarity-based classification of unit objectives, tasks, dialogues, and project activities according to the behavioral indicators of the 2022 Revised English Curriculum. Human verification was applied at the final coding stage, and Voyant Tools and AntConc were used for cross-validation. The results indicate that all three textbooks predominantly emphasize communication, while creativity is most salient in project-based tasks and collaboration in group-based activities and role plays. Publisher-level differences were also observed, with Visang showing the highest proportion of creativity-oriented tasks and Chunjae emphasizing collaboration more strongly. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of AI-assisted textbook analysis in reducing subjectivity and enhancing reproducibility. Despite the limited unit sample, this study provides a methodological foundation for future large-scale AI-based EFL materials research.

abstract_ko: This study examined Korean university EFL students’ perspectives on project-based learning (PBL) using AI tools in reading classes. Eighty students from two general English classes participated in a book-making project as a type of PBL, using ChatGPT as a language supporting tool. All participants completed a perception questionnaire after the project. Quantitative data were gathered through closed-ended questionnaires while qualitative data were collected through open-ended items. The research findings revealed that most students considered the reading project with ChatGPT beneficial for improving their English language skills, such as grammar, writing, speaking, and reading. Moreover, using AI for the project reduced anxiety and stress while increasing confidence. The results suggest that AI-enhanced PBL effectively integrates linguistic, cognitive, and affective dimensions of EFL learning, enabling students to engage in meaningful, personalized, and stress-free English practice. However, some students were concerned about overreliance on AI tools and the reliability of the information obtained from them. Overall, the study suggests that while the project can significantly influence language learning experiences, it is also important to address potential challenges. Considering the pedagogical implications discussed in this study, effective use of AI tools in the English language classes should be approached with careful consideration in the future.

abstract_ko: This study reviews domestic and international research on AI-based and multimodal feedback in English writing education, focusing on their key characteristics, learning effects, and pedagogical value. It explores how these feedback types help overcome the limitations of traditional feedback, such as time demands and lack of immediacy, while complementing each other to promote learner engagement. AI-based feedback, powered by natural language processing and machine learning, offers immediate, personalized, and repeatable responses that promote grammatical accuracy, language awareness, and self-regulated revision. Multimodal feedback, provided through audio, video, or screencast, combines verbal and visual cues to clarify meaning, increase motivation, and foster a stronger sense of connection between teachers and students. Integrating these two types of feedback can create a balanced feedback ecology that supports both cognitive precision and emotional engagement. Ultimately, their success depends on feedback literacy, the capacity of teachers and learners to interpret and apply feedback critically. By reframing feedback as an interactive and learner-centered process of reflection and knowledge construction rather than a corrective act, this study highlights the pedagogical importance of cultivating feedback literacy. It also calls for further research on hybrid feedback practices considering learner factors such as self-efficacy and digital competence across diverse contexts.

abstract_ko: 本研究は、Gather Town 授業を対面授業と比較した学習者の意見を分析し、相互作用の様相における差異を明らかにするとともに、教授․学習設計上の示唆を導き出した。Gather Town では、仮想空間という特性により学習に適した空間を提供することが可能であり、対面授業では容易ではない模擬体験を実現することができた。また、このように提供された空間を移動する経験は、学習活動への興味を高め、適切な強制性を与え、学習者の能動的な参加を促すことが明らかになった。対面授業と比較を通じ、このような｢空間構成の柔軟性｣がメタバース授業の第一の長所として浮彫りになった。 なお、アバターの活動は、より親密な相互作用を求める学習者には人見知りを和らげ、心理的距離を縮める効果をもたらし、対面状況における相互作用に負担を感じる学習者には、適切な距離感を確保することで安心感を与えることが示された。対面授業と比較を通じ、このような｢アバター媒介の相互作用｣がメタバース授業の第二の長所として浮彫りになった。 一方、Gather Town では、手書き文字を見せたり、微妙な表情や身振りなどの非言語的手がかりをキャッチしにくく、インターネット接続の問題や音声遅延といった技術的制約があることも確認された。また、メタバースを用いた授業はリアルタイム型のオンライン授業であるものの、Zoomなどの会議用プラットフォームを用いた授業よりも相互作用が多く生じるため、マイクを使用し、音声による発話が可能な場所を確保する必要があることを、事前に十分周知する必要があることも明らかとなった。 本研究を通して、第一に、対面状況とは異なる空間的特性を考慮した相互作用設計の必要性、第二に、学習者は適切な強制性のもとで、より安定的に授業および学習活動に集中できるということ、第三に、教室内には関係性や相互作用に対する態度の異なる学習者が共存しているため、それらを考慮した教授․学習設計が求められるということを、相互作用促進の観点から教授者が考慮すべき教育的示唆として導出した。

title_ko: The Role of Translation-Assisted ChatGPT Engagement in Enhancing Grammar Proficiency: Insights from TOEIC Performance
title_en: The Role of Translation-Assisted ChatGPT Engagement in Enhancing Grammar Proficiency:Insights from TOEIC Performance
kw_ko: ChatGPT(챗GPT); Grammar Learning(문법학습); TOEIC (토익); Artificial Intelligence(인공지능); Language Education(언어교육); Translation Experience (번역경험)
abstract_ko: This study investigates the potential of ChatGPT-assisted learning for improving English grammar proficiency among undergraduate students. Over a semester-long course, students engaged in translation tasks, grammar explanations, and sentence correction activities using ChatGPT, and their engagement patterns were compared to standardized TOEIC-based grammar test outcomes. The analysis examined relationships among ChatGPT utilization, translation experience, future intention to use AI tools, and grammar performance. Results showed that higher levels of ChatGPT utilization were moderately to strongly associated with improved grammar scores (r = .55), with each one-point increase in utilization predicting an estimated 8.3-point gain in TOEIC grammar performance (R² = .31). Translation experience also demonstrated a positive association, while future intention to use ChatGPT exhibited only a weak relationship with actual achievement. These findings highlight the pedagogical value of structured, active engagement with AI tools and underscore the need for instructional designs that balance AI support with learner autonomy to prevent over-reliance and promote sustained language development.
